title: Field triage (START)
stem: Tabletop. A double-decker bus has overturned on a highway. You are the medical officer at the casualty clearing point with one nurse. The sector officer brings you casualty cards one at a time. Triage each casualty with START and name any life-saving intervention.
notes:
Checked against START (Simple Triage and Rapid Treatment, Newport Beach 1983; used by many services including Hong Kong teaching), the SALT consensus (US 2008), and the UK NHS Ten Second Triage (TST, 2013), which replaced the triage sieve in the UK.

START in order: (1) Can walk → GREEN (minor). (2) Not breathing → open the airway once; still apnoeic → BLACK (dead/expectant); breathes → RED. (3) RR over 30 → RED. (4) Radial pulse absent or capillary refill over 2 seconds → RED (control bleeding). (5) Cannot follow simple commands → RED. (6) Otherwise → YELLOW (delayed). Only two interventions are allowed during triage: open the airway and control catastrophic haemorrhage (tourniquet/pressure); then move on in about 30 seconds per casualty. Triage is dynamic — re-triage at every stage. Children: JumpSTART uses RR 15–45 and five rescue breaths for the apnoeic child with a pulse. The UK TST puts catastrophic bleeding first and uses RR under 10 or over 30 as P1.

Your notes list 'Disaster/triage' as a topic only; no conflict. If your hospital uses TST or SALT instead, the logic is similar but the order and cut-offs differ slightly.

Perfect script checked against START triage, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. Removed the wrong categories and CPR in triage.

steps.label: Casualty 1
steps.hint: Man, 40, walking about holding a bleeding forearm; talking.

opts.t: Casualty 1: GREEN: walking wounded; direct to the minor area

steps.label: Casualty 2
steps.hint: Woman, 30, lying still, not breathing. Airway opened with a jaw thrust: she starts breathing, RR 12.

opts.t: Casualty 2: RED: breathes only after airway opening; place in recovery position

steps.label: Casualty 3
steps.hint: Man, 60, not breathing. Airway opened: still no breathing.

opts.t: Casualty 3: BLACK: apnoeic after airway opening; move on (no CPR in triage)

steps.label: Casualty 4
steps.hint: Teenager lying down, RR 36, radial pulse present.

steps.label: Casualty 5
steps.hint: Woman, 50, cannot stand, RR 24, capillary refill 4 s, spurting thigh wound.

opts.t: Casualty 5: RED: poor perfusion; apply a tourniquet above the wound first

steps.label: Casualty 6
steps.hint: Man, 35, cannot walk (deformed thigh), RR 20, radial pulse strong, refill 1.5 s, obeys commands.

steps.label: Casualty 7
steps.hint: Woman, 70, RR 18, radial pulse present, refill 1.5 s, eyes open but does not follow 'squeeze my hand'.

opts.t: Casualty 7: RED: cannot follow simple commands
Re-triage everyone at the clearing station (secondary triage, e.g. RTS)
Report to control: 4 RED, 1 YELLOW, 1 GREEN, 1 BLACK
Transport REDs first, spread across hospitals

wrong: Start CPR and give rescue breaths to every apnoeic casualty

qs.a: CRT over 2 s or no radial pulse
wrong: Heart rate over 120 per minute at the scene

badge.flavor: Walk, breathe, rate, refill, commands. 30 seconds each.

script.say: Casualty 1: GREEN: walking wounded; direct to the minor area.
Casualty 2: RED: breathes only after airway opening; place in recovery position.
Casualty 3: BLACK: apnoeic after airway opening; move on (no CPR in triage).
Casualty 5: RED: poor perfusion; apply a tourniquet above the wound first.
Casualty 7: RED: cannot follow simple commands.
Re-triage everyone at the clearing station (secondary triage, e.g. RTS). Report to control: 4 RED, 1 YELLOW, 1 GREEN, 1 BLACK. Transport REDs first, spread across hospitals.
